analysis.investment_thesis: Super Iron Foundry is a cyclical castings exporter with weak returns (ROE 6.2%, ROCE 7.41%) trading at an unjustified P/E of 25.4x — the quality doesn't match the multiple. This sits outside my circle of competence (consumer/retail/FMCG) and fails my basic return-on-capital thresholds.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 70.88% indicates skin in the game
Long operating history since 1988 with export exposure
Small market cap (INR 66 Cr) leaves room if business transforms
key_risks: ROE of 6.2% is well below my 15% threshold for quality businesses
P/E of 25.4x is expensive relative to single-digit returns on capital
Castings & forgings is commodity-linked and cyclical, not a predictable consumer franchise
red_flags: Earnings yield (~4%) lower than fixed deposit — capital destruction at current price
ROCE of 7.41% barely covers cost of capital
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I build conviction in boring, steady compounders in retail, FMCG, and financial services — businesses where demand is predictable and capital efficiency is high. Super Iron Foundry is a small industrial castings exporter, a cyclical commodity-adjacent business exposed to global industrial demand, steel input costs, and currency swings. ROE of 6.2% and ROCE of 7.41% are simply unacceptable for a core holding; the business isn't earning meaningfully above its cost of capital.

At INR 44.30 and a P/E of 25.4x, the market is paying a premium multiple for sub-par returns — the opposite of what value investing demands. I would need to see ROE sustainably above 15%, a clean debt profile, and a demonstrable franchise to even consider this. Without those, and given my preference to concentrate in deeply understood consumer businesses, this is an easy pass. AVOID.
